title: HttpInspectorContract
description: Root wrapper keeps every public v1 exchange and protocol definition in one JSON Schema artifact.

AddressDetails.description: Captures one endpoint and its origin without fabricating network resolution details.

BodyAvailability.description: Describes body availability before choosing where captured bytes are stored.

BodyContent.description: Body storage is opaque to the webview when content is retained outside the inline envelope.

ByteCount.description: A byte count follows the same explicit known/unknown rule as duration values.

CaptureFidelity.description: Every independently captured area advertises fidelity so Raw and Overview remain honest.

CaptureMessage.description: Lifecycle payloads accepted after a completed handshake.

CaptureProvenance.description: Identifies how a value was observed without claiming unavailable proxy-level data.

CaptureSource.description: Identifies the adapter process that emitted an exchange.

CaptureUiDelta.description: Batches can be safely applied by any UI adapter without sending full captured bodies hot-path.

ClientHello.description: The required first message from an adapter before capture telemetry is accepted.

CorrelationContext.description: Stable tracing fields are modelled now even though the first UI only displays them.

DatabaseCaptureAvailability.description: Availability is explicit so an unsafe value is never mistaken for an empty captured value.

DatabaseCommand.description: Canonical database command detail stored separately from HTTP exchanges.

DatabaseCommandFailure.description: Provider failures are separate from ordinary result metadata and remain visible in the database inspector.

DatabaseCommandKey.description: The pair prevents different monitored processes from colliding on a database command ID.

DatabaseCommandSummary.description: UI streaming remains small by sending a command summary instead of its query and parameter values.

DatabaseParameter.description: One database parameter preserves provider metadata without assuming every value is serializable.

DatabaseParameterCapture.description: Command-level parameter availability distinguishes a known empty parameter list from unavailable capture.

DatabaseQueryCapture.description: Keeps the original SQL intact when it is safe to retain, with a reason when it is not.

DatabaseResultAvailability.description: Captured result data is bounded and explicit so passive provider diagnostics remain valid.

DatabaseUiDelta.description: Database UI deltas are deliberately independent from the HTTP capture delta contract.

DurationValue.description: A duration is present only when known; provenance explains its source instead of using zero.

ExchangeFailure.description: Failure describes capture or transport failures, not ordinary 4xx and 5xx HTTP responses.

ExchangeKey.description: The pair prevents different monitored processes from colliding on an adapter exchange ID.

ExchangeLifecycle.description: Lifecycle semantics are independent from HTTP response status classes.

HeaderEntry.description: Retains header duplication and arrival order; no values are transformed or masked.

HelloAccepted.description: The inspector response after a successful protocol negotiation.

HelloError.description: Machine-readable handshake or message failures for adapters.

HttpBody.description: Captured body descriptors preserve the data supplied by an adapter without value redaction.

HttpExchange.description: The authoritative model stored by the capture hub and fetched by the inspector UI.

HttpExchangeSummary.description: UI streaming remains small by sending this projection instead of body content in every delta.

ProtocolRange.description: Inclusive protocol range advertised by an adapter during the initial handshake.

QueryEntry.description: Retains query duplication, original order, and a distinction between absent and empty values.

SchemaVersion.description: Contract compatibility version negotiated between an adapter and the inspector.

ServerMessage.description: All server messages retain an explicit v1 discriminator for language-neutral adapters.
